tools.name: Android SDK Platform Tools
tools.summary: The official ADB and Fastboot executables for Windows, macOS, and Linux.
notes: Fastboot is included in the same package as ADB.
DroidCrate verifies this archive before use in Stage 4.
No installer is required; the archive is extracted to a local folder.

tools.name: Android Flash Tool
tools.summary: Google's browser-based flasher for supported Pixel and development devices.
notes: Requires a Chromium-based browser and USB debugging.
Only devices with official factory images are supported.
The tool downloads images from Google directly; DroidCrate never hosts them.
tools.warning: Flashing erases the device. Back up first and use the exact model image.

tools.name: Google USB Driver
tools.summary: The official Windows driver for Nexus, Pixel, and Android development devices.
notes: Most phones expose ADB without this driver, but Fastboot often needs it.
Install it through Device Manager by choosing the extracted driver folder.

tools.name: Samsung Smart Switch
tools.summary: Samsung's official desktop app, which also installs the Samsung USB driver.
notes: Install this before using Odin or ADB with a Samsung phone.
It can back up photos, contacts, and messages without root.

tools.name: Odin
tools.summary: Samsung's service flashing utility for Download Mode, distributed through service channels.
notes: There is no official public download page for Odin.
Use Samsung Smart Switch for official updates whenever possible.
Firmware files must match the exact model and region.
tools.warning: Wrong firmware or the wrong CSC can brick the phone. Never flash a file from an unknown mirror.

tools.name: Heimdall
tools.summary: An open-source, cross-platform replacement for Odin on supported Samsung devices.
notes: Command-line tool; there is no guided interface.
Device support varies and newer Samsung bootloaders may refuse it.
Use the official release archive, not a repackaged build.
tools.warning: Advanced tool. A wrong partition name can destroy the bootloader.

tools.name: SP Flash Tool
tools.summary: MediaTek's service tool for low-level flashing over BROM and preloader modes.
notes: There is no official public download page.
It is usually used together with a scatter file and a full firmware package.
Newer MediaTek devices may require an authorised service account.
tools.warning: Format All + Download can erase the IMEI and calibration data permanently.

tools.name: QFIL (Qualcomm Flash Image Loader)
tools.summary: Qualcomm's service loader for Emergency Download (EDL) mode.
notes: QFIL is distributed through Qualcomm service channels, not a public download.
Requires the correct firehose programmer and raw program XML files.
EDL access may be blocked on newer bootloaders.
tools.warning: A mismatched programmer or storage size can hard-brick the device.

tools.name: Mi Flash Tool
tools.summary: Xiaomi's official Windows flasher for Fastboot ROM packages.
notes: There is no official public download page for the flasher itself.
Fastboot ROMs are published on Xiaomi's official download pages.
Do not select 'clean all and lock' unless you are certain.
tools.warning: Relocking the bootloader with modified firmware can brick the device.

tools.name: MSM Download Tool
tools.summary: A service tool for restoring OPPO, Realme, and OnePlus phones over EDL.
notes: The tool is tied to specific model packages and is not publicly distributed.
Many packages are region- and carrier-locked.
Official service centres can restore a device without third-party files.
tools.warning: Using a package for another model can permanently erase the device identity.

tools.name: LGUP
tools.summary: LG's service flashing tool for KDZ firmware packages.
notes: LGUP is a service tool without a public official download.
Some versions require a model-specific DLL.
LG has ended phone production; official service options are limited.
tools.warning: Refurbish mode erases all user data and can fail during a power cut.

tools.name: TWRP
tools.summary: The most widely used open-source custom recovery, with device-specific builds.
notes: Only install a build published for your exact model.
A custom recovery usually requires an unlocked bootloader.
Keep a copy of the stock boot image before making changes.
tools.warning: An incompatible recovery image can prevent the phone from booting.

tools.name: OrangeFox Recovery
tools.summary: An open-source custom recovery focused on a modern interface and extra tools.
notes: Builds are device-specific; check the codename carefully.
Some builds are unofficial and are marked as such on the site.
Use the official site rather than a file-sharing mirror.
tools.warning: Requires an unlocked bootloader. Encryption support varies by build.

tools.name: Magisk
tools.summary: The standard systemless root solution, with modules and a hidden root manager.
notes: Patching the boot image is usually safer than flashing a pre-rooted ROM.
Keep the original boot image for OTA updates and recovery.
Banking and payment apps may refuse to run on rooted devices.
tools.warning: Rooting voids warranties and weakens the security model. Back up before patching.

tools.name: KernelSU
tools.summary: A kernel-based root solution for devices with a supported custom kernel.
notes: Requires a kernel built with KernelSU support, or a supported GKI image.
Not every phone has a compatible kernel.
The manager app is separate from the kernel patch.
tools.warning: Flashing the wrong boot or kernel image can leave the phone unbootable.

tools.name: APatch
tools.summary: A kernel-patching root method with a module system and per-app superuser control.
notes: Patches a boot image with a kernel module rather than using Magisk.
Compatibility depends on the device kernel and Android version.
Read the official compatibility notes before patching.
tools.warning: Experimental on many devices. Keep a bootable backup image.
